# homarr_root_certificate (Data Source)

Inspects a custom root CA certificate that Homarr trusts for its integrations, by the file name it has in Homarr's trusted-certificates folder. Useful in a `check` block, for example to warn before the CA expires.

~> **Requires Homarr 2.2.0 or newer**, which added `GET /api/certificates/{fileName}`, and an admin API key.

A file Homarr does not have is not an error: `found` is `false` and the other attributes are null. Homarr has no endpoint that lists certificates, so a file can only be looked up by its exact name. A file that exists but is not a single self-signed root CA — a chain or a leaf certificate added through the UI, for example — fails the read, as does a symlink or a file over 64 KiB. A Homarr started outside production mode without `LOCAL_CERTIFICATE_PATH` has no certificate folder and reports every file as not found.

The certificate itself is not managed here: Homarr's REST API can add one but cannot remove it, so a resource could not be destroyed.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Requires Homarr 2.2.0 or newer and an admin API key.
data "homarr_root_certificate" "corp" {
  file_name = "corp-root-ca.crt"
}

# Warn a month before the CA Homarr trusts for its integrations expires. A
# missing file is not an error: found is false.
check "corp_root_ca" {
  assert {
    condition     = data.homarr_root_certificate.corp.found
    error_message = "Homarr does not trust corp-root-ca.crt."
  }

  # A conditional rather than ||: Terraform before 1.12 evaluates both sides of
  # ||, and timecmp fails on the null valid_to of a missing file.
  assert {
    condition = data.homarr_root_certificate.corp.found ? timecmp(
      data.homarr_root_certificate.corp.valid_to,
      timeadd(plantimestamp(), "720h"),
    ) > 0 : true
    error_message = "corp-root-ca.crt expires within 30 days."
  }
}

# Confirm Homarr holds exactly the file you distributed.
output "corp_root_ca_matches" {
  value = data.homarr_root_certificate.corp.sha256 == sha256(file("${path.module}/corp-root-ca.crt"))
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `file_name` (String) File name of the certificate in Homarr's trusted-certificates folder, such as `corp-root-ca.crt`. Homarr accepts at most 128 characters: a letter or digit, then letters, digits, `.`, `_` or `-`, ending in `.crt` or `.pem`.

### Read-Only

- `ca` (Boolean) Always `true` for a certificate Homarr reports, since it only reports root CAs. Null when `found` is `false`.
- `fingerprint256` (String) SHA-256 fingerprint of the certificate, as upper-case hex pairs separated by colons. Null when `found` is `false`.
- `found` (Boolean) Whether Homarr has a certificate file with this name.
- `sha256` (String) SHA-256 of the file's bytes as lower-case hex, e.g. to compare with `sha256(file("corp-root-ca.crt"))`. Null when `found` is `false`.
- `valid_from` (String) Start of the certificate's validity, as an RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC. Null when `found` is `false`.
- `valid_to` (String) End of the certificate's validity, as an RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC; compare it with `timecmp`. An expired certificate is still reported. Null when `found` is `false`.
